# dynamodb

DynamoDB access patterns - Query over Scan, key conditions, bounded reads - plus table posture (PITR, deletion protection) from dumps.

## Detected anti-patterns

### `AF-DATA-009` — DynamoDB Scan without limit or filter (high)

Scan reads every item in the table before filtering — RCU cost and latency grow with table size, not with the result set. The call site shows no Limit, FilterExpression or IndexName argument.


Remediation: Prefer Query on a key condition; if Scan is required, bound it with Limit and a FilterExpression, and keep it off request paths.

Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Scan.html

### `AF-DATA-010` — DynamoDB Query without a key condition (medium)

Query without KeyConditionExpression degenerates toward a scan over the partition — the declared kwargs carry no key condition.


Remediation: Pass KeyConditionExpression with the partition key (and sort key when modeled).

Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Query.html

### `AF-STORE-001` — DynamoDB table has point-in-time recovery disabled (high)

`PointInTimeRecoveryStatus` absent from ENABLED means an accidental delete or corrupting write is unrecoverable past the last on-demand backup — the continuous-backups API answers it directly.

Remediation: Enable PITR (`UpdateContinuousBackups`) on tables holding state the business cannot rebuild; 35 days of rollback costs little against a lost table.

Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/PointInTimeRecovery.html

### `AF-STORE-002` — DynamoDB table has deletion protection off (medium)

`DeletionProtectionEnabled` false leaves the table one API call away from destruction — cheap insurance against the worst typo.

Remediation: Enable deletion protection on tables whose recreation cost exceeds the operational friction of one extra flag.

Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/WorkingWithTables.Basics.html
